predecessors.name: Republic of Indonesia
predecessors.text: West Java, where Kartosoewirjo proclaimed the Islamic State of Indonesia on 7 August 1949 'in protest against the Renville Agreement'; 'the Darul Islam controlled one-third of West Java' in 1957.

successors.name: Republic of Indonesia
successors.text: South Sulawesi, where Abdul Kahar Muzakkar's rebels joined Darul Islam in 1951 and controlled more than 90 percent in 1957

ledger.x: 1949: Kartosoewirjo proclaims the Islamic State of Indonesia in West Java (7 August), 'in protest against the Renville Agreement, which ceded West Java to the Dutch'.
1949: the fighting in West Java begins; in 1957 the Darul Islam 'controlled one-third of West Java' with 15,000 armed guerrillas.
1951: South Sulawesi joins Darul Islam ('joined the Darul Islam movement in 1951'); the page gives no month.
1965: the Darul Islam insurgency ends in Indonesia; the land is the Republic's.

wars.name: Darul Islam rebellion
wars.outcome: The Republic crushed the movement region by region: South Kalimantan 1959, Aceh by negotiated peace 1959-1962, West Java in June-August 1962, South Sulawesi in February 1965.

certainty.note: Rebel-held rural land with guerrilla fronts; the page gives only 1957 estimates, no boundaries.
